// 2026-09-20: Retuned: the old rig was ONE white lamp almost straight overhead (height 3.0, intensity 0.75) — even, but flat and glaring, with no cast shadow to give the milled plates depth. Now a softbox KEY up-left at a moderate rake (height 1.05, so bevels and screws throw short, soft shadows down-right), a dim cool FILL from the right to keep the shadow side from going dead, and no third lamp. Intensities are down ~20% from before for a rig you can look at for an hour; the key's specular is raised a little and tightened so the brushed-aluminium grain shows through the highlight instead of the plate reading as flat grey. NOT animated — a moving lamp on a light skin is what made it hard to judge. Tune from here: KEY intensity is overall brightness, KEY height is shadow length (smaller = longer, harder), FILL intensity is how dark the shadows get.
